title: On Women Who Think They Regret Motherhood
author: Melissa Edgington
source: Your Mom Has A Blog (yourmomhasablog.com), September 22, 2026
summary: Melissa Edgington responds to a TikTok trend in which mothers list the reasons they regret having children. She rejects the reading that these women hate their children and instead diagnoses the trend as bondage to an idol of self, reinforced by modern feminist ideals and social media messaging that frames children as barriers to freedom and fulfillment. Her argument places the trend within a spiritual contest, casting the voice that says motherhood is holding women back as a continuation of the tempter's question in the garden. The essay's central move is to recast motherhood through the image of the shepherd, who stands bodily between the flock and harm. Edgington argues that motherhood is one of the few pursuits that matter to eternity, that its sacrifices are the means by which Christ forms women, and that the fleeting years with children are an opportunity that will not return.
points: Edgington argues that regretful mothers still love their children but have their love overshadowed by an idol of self.
She contends that the culture now treats selfishness and boundary-drawing as virtues, turning children into obstacles between women and leisure, careers and freedom.
The essay frames mothers as shepherds appointed to stand between their children and a hostile culture.
Motherhood is set against career, travel and comfort as one of the few things in life that matter to eternity.
quotes: I’ve seen podcasters frame this trend as women revealing that they hate their children. I disagree. These women love their children. But their love for their kids is being overshadowed by what I’m convinced is Satan’s most effective strategy to keep humans from flourishing, doing good, experiencing joy, or seeking God.
It’s practically become a virtue to be stingy and selfish, to draw boundaries, to seek what feels best for ourselves above all. In this culture, it’s a hard time to be a child.

Children have become the barrier between women and all of the things that seem appealing, all the things that seem fulfilling, all the things that keep us from “losing ourselves.” At least, this is what Satan wants us to believe.

God gave them to us and uniquely called us to shepherd them through this life, and it requires sacrifice. A shepherd fights what comes after his sheep with his bare hands, and God has given us a very similar job.

He doesn’t have to do anything more than convince us day by day through the influence of social media that shepherding our children is an inferior occupation, that it’s holding us back, that it’s making us less than we’re meant to be, that it’s not what we really want to do.
The kids aren’t the barriers to happiness. We fight our own joy with both arms flailing because it’s hard to lay your life down for another.

There aren’t that many things in this life that matter to eternity. Generally speaking, a career doesn’t, travel doesn’t, being free to eat a good lunch doesn’t, having nice furniture and a pretty house doesn’t. But motherhood does.
